slot.brief: Give two relations on a small set (shown via a diagram of ordered pairs/arrows); decide which standard properties (reflexive, symmetric, transitive) each relation satisfies.

stem: Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$. The relations $R$ and $S$ on $A$ are represented by arrows in the figure. Which statement is correct?
options: $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; $S$ is reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive.
$R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive; $S$ is reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive.
$R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric; $S$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric.
$R$ is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive; $S$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

verdicts.working: R has all loops plus 1↔2, so it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. S has all loops and arrows 1→2, 2→3; it is reflexive but not symmetric, and not transitive since 1→3 is absent.

working:
$R=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,1)\}$: all loops; each pair has its reverse; all required compositions are present. Hence $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. $S=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3)\}$: all loops, but $(1,2)$ has no reverse and $(1,2),(2,3)$ lack $(1,3)$. Hence $S$ is reflexive, neither symmetric nor transitive.

Independent check: R has all loops plus 1↔2, so it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. S has all loops and arrows 1→2, 2→3; it is reflexive but not symmetric, and not transitive since 1→3 is absent.
solution:
A relation is reflexive if it contains every loop, symmetric if each arrow has its reverse, and transitive if $a\to b$ and $b\to c$ imply $a\to c$.
$R$ has all loops and the arrows $1\leftrightarrow2$; all required compositions are present, so it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
$S$ has all loops, but $1\to2$ has no reverse, and $1\to2$, $2\to3$ occur without $1\to3$; hence it is neither symmetric nor transitive.

For R, draw a loop at each vertex, and draw arrows 1→2 and 2→1; draw no other arrows. For S, draw a loop at each vertex, and draw arrows 1→2 and 2→3; draw no other arrows. Make all arrowheads and loops clear.
